newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl comes to raise morale of flooded east Germany.
newsitem.headline: Kohl comes to raise morale of flooded east Germany.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl visited flood-stricken eastern Germany on Tuesday to boost the morale of residents, relief workers and soldiers as swollen rivers forced more evacuations across central Europe.

Hundreds of emergency workers on both the German and Polish banks of the Oder River battled to reinforce sodden dikes and prevent further flooding with another surge of water expected in the next 24 hours.

Floods caused by heavy rain also forced 800 people out of their homes in the Lvov region in western Ukraine and the evacuation of more than 1,000 in Romania, where the Danube delta region was particularly badly hit.

Kohl tried to reassure inhabitants of the flood-threatened village of Altreetz that troops were doing everything possible to reinforce dikes protecting the fertile Oderbruch area, which lies below the level of the river.

He defended efforts by 9,000 soldiers to build up a second line of dikes to secure larger towns while angry villagers accused authorities of being ready to let their homes flood to save the bigger communities.

"There are so many soldiers working on the secondary dike. We believe there is not enough being done to save the main dike," Helga Scholz, mayor of the village of Alt Maedewitz, told Kohl as angry local residents watched.

Kohl insisted the villagers' homes were not being abandoned. "I have come here to tell you that the army has orders to hold the main line of dikes," he told Scholz in Altreetz, where sandbags littered the main square.
"I haven't come here for nothing," Kohl said emphatically, his hand on the mayor's shoulder.

Kohl earlier stressed to residents in the town of Bad Freienwalde that defending the area was a task for the whole nation and demonstrated the solidarity between west and east Germans, seven years after the unification of the country.
"The main thing I want to say, in this first natural disaster seven years after unification, is that we not only express ourselves in words but also in deeds," he said.
"We want to ensure that people here feel our compassion in a special way. This is a national task."

The Brandenburg state interior ministry started mass inoculations against typhoid and jaundice as an extra precaution in case drinking water had become infected, and it called on 5,000 people to report for injections.
Authorities in the Polish town of Slubice, across the river from Germany's Frankfurt an der Oder, said eroded dikes there could still yield to the river.

Elsewhere in Poland, flood waters receded and weather forecasts were for more sunshine and only occasional showers, although almost 2,000 sq km were still under water and almost 40,000 people remained displaced.
In Romania, where flooding last month killed 12 people in the region of Bihor, weather forecasters said conditions would improve in the next 24 hours, with only occasional showers in mountain areas.
Newly-appointed Prime Minister Valery Pustovoitenko was due to visit Ukraine's flood area on Wednesday.
In Germany, farming officials said the recent floods had cost farmers 50 million marks ($27.2 million) already and losses could multiply if main dikes protecting the Oderbruch plateau burst.
The floods have claimed more than 100 lives in neighbouring Poland and the Czech Republic.
Germany has so far escaped the worst of the damage. But thousands of people have already been evacuated from their homes and thousands more are on standby.

Kohl, who flew in from an Austrian vacation resort dressed in a casual suede jacket, said federal and state governments were already thinking about how best to repair the Oder dikes before the annual high water arrived in the autumn.

Paying his second visit to the region, Kohl said the government planned to let the army stay throughout the summer to ensure repairs were completed by the autumn. He said it might be time to erect more modern flood protection. ($ = 1.836 German Marks)
